title: Cost + Latency Operational Synthesis Workflow
author: Marcus Chen
content:
Summary:
This document defines the operational workflow and runbook for synthesizing cost signals with latency/SLI telemetry to rapidly triage and remediate incidents that affect both unit economics and user experience. It is aimed at platform operators and oncall engineers responsible for the runtime-router, batch-aggregator, kv-prefix-cache, and token-accounting-service.

Why this exists:
- Operators frequently see cost alerts (token burn, GPU minutes spike) and latency SLO burn separately; root causes are often correlated and require a single, repeatable synthesis workflow.
- Reducing mean time to safe-action preserves both customer experience and economic SLAs (hosted pricing tiers + Dedicated commitments).

Goals and scope:
- Detect correlated cost + latency incidents within 3 minutes of onset.
- Provide a decision ladder that prioritizes low-risk, high-impact mitigations (throttles, routing changes, model variant degrade) before capacity additions.
- Produce a post-incident artifact with cost delta and p50/p95/p99 impact calculations for billing and product QBR.
- Applies to production-hosted and dedicated clusters; for Private deployments follow the same steps but use customer-specific telemetry endpoints.

Owner and escalation:
- Primary owner: Platform Observability (oncall rotation: platform-observability@redwood.com).
- Secondary owner: Runtime Ops.
- Escalation: if SLO burn > 30% and cost spike > 3x baseline for 30m, page the Platform Incident Response Pager.

Quick reference SLOs and thresholds:
- Latency SLO (foreground requests): p95 < 220ms, error rate < 0.5%
- Cost guard: rolling 1h token cost per tenant > 3x baseline or global token/minutes > 2x baseline.
- Alerting severity mapping:
  - Sev3: single-model p95 > 350ms for 5m or token spike 2x baseline for 10m.
  - Sev2: cross-tenant p95 > 450ms or global token/minutes > 3x baseline for 15m.
  - Sev1: sustained SLO breach with customer-impacting errors or billing runaways.

Detection: signals and dashboards to open first
1) Open the "Cost-Latency Synthesis" dashboard (dashboards/Cost-Latency-Synthesis). Widgets: top tenants by token burn, p95 heatmap by model, GPU minutes over last 2h, request queue depth, kv-prefix-cache hit ratio, routing-fallback-rate.
2) Run these quick queries (examples):
   - PromQL: 
     sum by (tenant) (rate(token_emitted_total[5m]))
     -> top 20 tenants, compare to 1w baseline from metrics_store.
   - PromQL latency slice: 
     histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, service, model))
   - SQL (cost ledger): 
     SELECT tenant_id, SUM(tokens) as tokens_1h FROM token_ledger WHERE recorded_at > now() - interval '1 hour' GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY tokens_1h DESC LIMIT 20;
3) Open traces for the highest-latency model variant in the trace UI and check for: garbage-collection stalls, kernel-queueing, repeated retry loops, or heavy KV cache misses.

Immediate triage checklist (first 10 minutes)
1) Confirm whether cost spike and latency spike overlap in time and tenant set. If they are disjoint, treat independently.
2) If overlap exists, determine scope: single-tenant, multi-tenant shard, or global. Check: routing_shard_id, region, instance_type.
3) Annotate incident with the correlated-tenants list and top three models consuming tokens.
4) Apply the lowest-impact mitigations first (safe-action ladder below).

Safe-action ladder (ordered by safety and reversibility)
1) Soft throttle: apply a 20% soft-token-rate throttle on the offending tenant(s) via rate-control-api. Monitor effect for 2 minutes.
   - Command example: curl -X POST https://control-plane/_admin/rate-control -d '{"tenant":"T-1234","throttle_pct":20,"ttl_s":300}'
2) Switch to cheap model variant: update routing rules to route <1% sample traffic to the lower-cost variant and monitor quality/regression guard rails.
3) Enable KV-prefix-cache prefetch for hot prefixes if cache hit ratio < 70% (safe to enable incrementally).
   - Toggle example: /ops/cache-toggle --prefix hot_prefixes --action prefetch --window 60s
4) Autoscale burst (reserved) for Dedicated customers only: apply controlled capacity-burst for a single region with rollback TTL 30m. This requires an approval step if projected cost > $Xk/h (see escalation).
5) Model swap / degrade globally: move traffic from large decoder model to a smaller quantized variant (last resort). Must run a quick A/B quality check sample set in the sandbox and notify product.

When to immediately escalate to Sev1:
- Cost continues to grow after two safe-action steps and p95 remains > 2x SLO for 20m.
- Anomalous token patterns that suggest infinite-loop prompts (detect repeated prompt token sequences > 5x).
- Significant customer-facing errors (500s, malformed responses).

Automated detection rules (recommended alert definitions)
- Alert A (Cost-Latency Correlate): fires when (global_token_rate/rolling_baseline) > 2.5 AND global_p95_latency > 1.5 * target_p95 for 10m. Severity: Sev2.
- Alert B (Tenant Token Runaway): tenant_token_rate > 5x tenant_weekly_baseline for 15m -> page runtime-ops. Severity: Sev2.
- Alert C (KV Erosion): kv_prefix_cache_hit_ratio < 60% AND p95_increase > 30ms for a model shard -> trigger cache-prefetch job. Severity: Sev3.

Example alert YAML (for the alerting system):
- name: cost_latency_correlate
  expr: |
    (sum(rate(token_emitted_total[5m])) / sum(avg_over_time(token_emitted_total[1h][1h]))) > 2.5 and
    (histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)) > 0.0015)
  for: 10m
  labels: { severity: "sev2", owner: "platform-observability" }
  annotations: { runbook: "/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/cost-latency-operational-synthesis-workflow-2026" }

Remediation templates and command snippets
- Soft throttle (see above).
- Model variant route flip (safe sample example):
  PATCH /routing/v1/policy/{policy_id}
  body: {"rules":[{"match":{"model":"gptx-large"},"action":{"traffic_split":{"gptx-quantized":0.95,"gptx-small":0.05}}}],"comment":"Emergency degrade 2026-06-09"}
- Cache prefetch job: opsctl cache prefetch --shard s-12 --limit 5000 --background
- Temporary capacity burst (Dedicated only): billing-tagged ops request: /ops/capacity/burst --region us-west-2 --gpus 8 --reason "cost-latency mitigate" --ttl 1800

Data to collect for post-incident artifact (minimum):
- Incident ID and timeline with annotated dashboards/screenshots.
- Delta in tokens consumed (1h window pre vs post), delta in GPU minutes, and estimated incremental cost in dollars.
- Latency SLI curves (p50/p95/p99) pre, during, post.
- Actions taken, who approved, and time-to-effect for each.
- Regression checks (sampled outputs compared to golden prompts) if model variant changed.

Post-incident analysis (24–72 hours) steps:
1) Triage meeting with platform-observability, runtime-ops, and product-analytics to validate root cause hypothesis.
2) Compute unit economics: additional cost / recoverable revenue opportunity and recommend permanent controls (quota, routing policy, SLI weight change).
3) Add or tune an automatic mitigation (e.g., auto-throttle rule or tenant soft-cap) if a repeat pattern is detected.
4) Create a retro artifact: one-page summary, severity, customer impact, and a 90-day follow-up checklist (owner, deadline).

Recommended dashboards and panels (minimum set)
- Cost-Latency overview: top-left timeline with p95 and token rate overlay.
- Tenant explosion table: top 50 tenants with token/min and p95.
- Model heatmap: p95 by model x region.
- Kernel queue depth and GPU utilization for top 10 hosts.
- KV hit ratio and cache misses by prefix shard.

Synthesis playbook tips and anti-patterns
- Tip: Always validate token accounting against the ledger (token_ledger) before applying billing-impacting actions. Ledger data has canonical finality after 15m.
- Tip: Use a 2-minute sample window after soft-throttle changes before moving to the next step. Most token runaway issues stabilize quickly.
- Anti-pattern: Immediately spinning up large amounts of capacity without trying throttles or degraded variants — this often increases cost without fixing the root request pattern.

Appendix: example PromQL snippets to copy
- Top tenants by recent token rate:
  topk(20, sum by (tenant) (rate(token_emitted_total[5m])))
- Global p95 time series:
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
- GPU minutes (per host):
  sum(rate(gpu_time_seconds_total[5m])) by (host) / 60

If this workflow misses edge cases or your runbook steps failed during an incident, open a ticket in #platform-ops and assign to platform-observability. For improvements, propose changes and add reviewers from runtime-ops and product-analytics.
